findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plaintext static credentials. User data is readable through the instance metadata service (including via SSRF on the internet-facing web server) and is stored unencrypted in the EC2 API and in Terraform state.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true that is routed to an internet gateway, and is attached to a security group permitting 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 22 and 80, making it directly reachable from the internet with no network boundary.

No metadata_options block with http_tokens = "required" is set, so IMDSv1 remains available. Combined with the secrets embedded in user data and the public reachability of the host, an SSRF flaw in the web application would allow trivial retrieval of metadata and the embedded credentials.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance root volume may be created without EBS encryption, leaving data at rest unprotected unless account-level default encryption is enabled.
Ingress allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts against a publicly addressed host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 with no TLS/HTTPS listener configured anywhere in the configuration, so all web traffic to and from the host traverses the internet in cleartext.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unconstrained outbound channel for data exfiltration or command-and-control if the internet-facing host is compromised.
The EBS volume attached to the web host is created without encrypted = true and without a KMS key, so data written to the attached storage is stored unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted volume and no encryption is configured, so a full unencrypted copy of the volume contents persists in snapshot storage where it can be shared or restored.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so network flow records revealing internal addressing and traffic patterns are stored without enforced encryption.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, restrictive ACL, or bucket policy is defined, so protection of the flow log data from accidental public ACL/policy exposure relies entirely on account-level defaults.
No bucket policy denying requests with aws:SecureTransport = false is attached, so flow log objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.

force_destroy = true is set and no versioning or MFA delete is configured on the audit log destination bucket, so flow log evidence can be silently deleted or overwritten by an attacker covering their tracks.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true, combined with the route table association to the internet gateway, gives every instance launched here a public IP and direct internet exposure by default.
